title: Kinetic proofreading in receptor signaling (Hlavacek et al., 2001)
reference: Hlavacek WS, Redondo A, Metzger H, Wofsy C, Goldstein B (2001). Kinetic proofreading models for cell signaling predict ways to escape kinetic proofreading. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 98:7295-7300. doi:10.1073/pnas.121172298. See also Hlavacek WS, Redondo A, Wofsy C, Goldstein B (2002). Kinetic proofreading in receptor-mediated transduction of cellular signals: receptor aggregation, partially activated receptors, and cytosolic messengers. Bull Math Biol 64:887-911. doi:10.1006/bulm.2002.0306

kp__FREE.note: each of the five modification steps, /s

notes: Published default parameterization (300,000 receptors, 602 ligands, N=5 modification steps). Hundreds of ligands and dimers, so the relative noise is moderate; the terminally modified dimer count (about 20) is the noisy observable and the one that carries kp, since the fraction of dimers that complete all five steps scales as (kp/(kp+2*koff))^5.
